title: Filing a First Information Report (FIR)
subtitle: Step-by-step guide to reporting a cognizable offense to Pakistani police

steps.title: Reporting to the Police Station
steps.whatTheLawSays: Under Section 154 CrPC, the Station House Officer (SHO) is legally bound to record an FIR immediately when information regarding a cognizable offense is presented, whether orally or in writing.
steps.whereToGo: The local Police Station (Thana) having territorial jurisdiction over the place of incident.
steps.whatToFile: Written complaint detailing the date, time, place of incident, names/descriptions of accused, and witness details.
steps.cost: Free of cost. Demanding money for registering an FIR is illegal.
steps.ifRefused: If the SHO refuses to record the FIR, submit a written application to the Superintendent of Police (SP) or Justice of Peace (Ex-officio Sessions Judge under Section 22-A/22-B CrPC).

steps.title: Verification and Signature
steps.whatTheLawSays: The recorded statement must be read over to the informant and signed or thumb-imprinted by them to verify accuracy before entry into the police register (Form 5.24).
steps.whereToGo: Duty Officer / Station House Officer (SHO) office within the police station.
steps.whatToFile: Your signed or thumb-imprinted statement as recorded by the officer.
steps.ifRefused: Do not sign if the statement recorded differs from your actual account. Request correct re-transcription.

steps.title: Obtaining a Certified Copy
steps.whatTheLawSays: The informant has an absolute legal right to receive a copy of the recorded FIR free of cost immediately after registration.
steps.whereToGo: Police Station Front Desk or Police Service Center (Khidmat Markaz).
steps.whatToFile: Request for official stamped copy of the registered FIR.
steps.ifRefused: File a complaint with the District Police Officer (DPO) or Ombudsman (Mohtasib).

title: Handling Illegal Tenant Eviction
subtitle: Legal protections for tenants against unlawful landlord eviction

steps.title: Notice Review and Response
steps.whatTheLawSays: Landlords must provide statutory notice and apply via the Rent Tribunal under relevant provincial rented premises acts.

citations.act: Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 / Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance 1979

steps.whatToFile: Written reply to eviction notice with rent payment receipts.
steps.cost: Varies based on court fee stamps.
steps.ifRefused: Seek stay order from the Rent Controller.

title: Filing for Khula (Dissolution of Marriage)
subtitle: Process for a woman seeking judicial dissolution of marriage

steps.title: Filing Family Suit
steps.whatTheLawSays: A Muslim wife is entitled to seek Khula through the Family Court subject to relinquishment of deferred Haq Mehr.
steps.whereToGo: Family Court in the district where the wife resides.
steps.whatToFile: Plaint for dissolution of marriage supported by affidavit and Nikahnama copy.
steps.ifRefused: Appeal against decree as per Family Court procedures.

title: Recovering Unpaid Wages & Salary
subtitle: Recourse for employees facing non-payment or delayed wages

steps.title: Filing Claim with Payment of Wages Authority
steps.whatTheLawSays: Employees can file claims against illegal wage deductions or non-payment within statutory timelines.
steps.whereToGo: Authority appointed under Payment of Wages Act / Labor Court.
steps.whatToFile: Claim application along with employment contract, appointment letter, and bank statements.
steps.cost: Exempted or minimal court fees for labor claims.
steps.ifRefused: File appeal before the Labor Appellate Tribunal.

title: Reporting Cyber Harassment & Blackmail
subtitle: Steps to register complaints with FIA Cybercrime Wing

steps.title: Submitting Cybercrime Complaint
steps.whatTheLawSays: Harassment, stalking, or blackmailing via electronic communications is a punishable offense under PECA.
steps.whereToGo: FIA Cyber Crime Reporting Center or online via NR3C Portal.
steps.whatToFile: Screenshots, URLs, phone numbers, and digital evidence.
steps.ifRefused: Lodge grievance with the Ministry of Interior or High Court writ petition.

steps.title: Production Before Magistrate
steps.whatTheLawSays: Every arrested person must be produced before the nearest Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest excluding journey time.
steps.whatToFile: Habeas corpus application or representation through legal counsel.
steps.ifRefused: File Habeas Corpus petition under Article 199 in High Court or Section 491 CrPC in Sessions Court.
